test_title: Delhi Police Constable (Executive) 2023 - GK/CA (Held on: 17 Nov, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: gk
question: Net national product at market price can be defined as:

options.text: Gross national product at market price plus depreciation
Net domestic product at market price plus net income from abroad
Net domestic product at market price minus net income from abroad
Net domestic product at market price minus depreciation

solution:
The correct answer is __**Net domestic product at market price plus net income from abroad**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• **Net National Product (NNP) at market price** is calculated by adjusting the Net Domestic Product (NDP) at market price with the net income from abroad.

• **Net income from abroad** includes the difference between the income residents earn from abroad and the income that foreigners earn within the domestic economy.

• The formula for NNP at market price is: **NNP at market price = NDP at market price + Net income from abroad**.

• It reflects the overall economic performance of a country considering both domestic and international income.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Gross National Product (GNP):**

• GNP is the total market value of all final goods and services produced by the residents of a country in a given period, usually a year.

• It includes the income earned by residents from abroad but excludes the income earned by foreigners within the domestic economy.

• **Net Domestic Product (NDP):**

• NDP is the total value of all final goods and services produced within a country in a given period, minus depreciation.

• It reflects the actual economic output, accounting for the wear and tear on the capital stock.

• **Depreciation:**

• Depreciation represents the reduction in the value of an asset over time due to wear and tear, age, or obsolescence.

• In national accounting, it is subtracted from the Gross Domestic Product (GDP) to calculate the NDP.

• **Net Income from Abroad:**

• It is the difference between the income earned by residents from their investments abroad and the income earned by foreigners from their investments in the domestic economy.

• This component is crucial in adjusting the domestic product to reflect the true economic performance of a nation on a global scale.
